justification: This round fixes two of round 1's three design majors cleanly and leaves the third genuinely open, so the score moves up from 7.6 but stays below the 8.5 pass bar. Fixed: (1) phone clipping — the flagship Add-vs-Insert(0) benchmark now puts `list.Add(i);` and `list.Insert(0, i);` on their own indented lines and both are fully visible at 390px; the `sizes` array wraps onto two visible lines; the `NsPerElement`/`SumRowFirst`/`SumColumnFirst` call sites and loop headers are legible; the `Report`/`Best` method signatures in the tiled-grid and jagged-grid programs sit on their own lines and are fully visible; output-panel wildcards are now spaced under their headers instead of glued to the preceding number. (2) The central cache-locality insight, which round 1 flagged as prose-only with no figure, now has Figure 4 (a cache-line reuse strip diagram): verified legible and correctly coloured in both mobile-dark and desktop-dark, its labels ('Row-first: next line, 64 B away', 'Column-first: next line is 16,000 B down, a whole row away', 'Back near the top only after n rows: that gap is the reuse distance') match the surrounding prose exactly, and it renders at a sensible size at 390px. Not fixed: reading rhythm / code walls. The 66-line opening harness (NsPerElement with warm-up and repetition arithmetic) still sits in front of the first result, and the 'Grids' section's layout benchmark (RectSum/JagSum/FlatSum plus a Report/Best wrapper, ~110 lines) is structurally unchanged from round 1 — each line is now legible, but the wall of near-identical scaffolding before the payoff is the same shape it was in round 1. That keeps this major open. A handful of new and carried-over minors round out the picture: the 'Picking between an array, a list and a view' comparison table hides its entire List<T> column on phone in both themes (confirmed on mobile-dark and mobile-light — the table box ends exactly at the T[] column with no visible List<T> header at all, which is worse than round 1's partially-cut Ratio column and is the actual point of the table); a few `Best(n, () => SumRows(g, ...))`-style call sites in the tiled and jagged-grid programs still clip their trailing arguments; the DropEvens exercise's `for` loop header clips `i++)` inside the narrower exercise-callout width; several `Console.WriteLine` header strings truncate mid-word on phone (cosmetic); and three round-1 minors (citations not linked to the numbered source list, no small figure for List<T> capacity growth, the mobile hero block eating most of the first screen) remain unaddressed. Lighthouse, console errors, broken links and mobile overflow are all clean (see below); the only report.json failure is the expected NEEDS_MARKUS placeholder.
